messages:
devon: quick heads-up — ran a bunch of eviction simulations overnight targeting GPU/CPU cache split (70/30) and saw intermittent OOM spikes during warmup traffic. suspect fragmentation + aggressive TTLs for prompt keys.

maria: curious — what workload distribution did you use? short prompts vs long context?

devon: mostly bursty PLG traffic: 80% short prompts (<64 tokens), 15% medium (64-256), 5% long. warmup traffic originated from canary routing (small fanout).

chris: can you paste the profiler summary? kernel selection might be flipping between cudnn kernels and our fallback kernels at certain seq lengths. that causes transient mem pressure.

devon: pasted profiler snippet: 
```
[profile] total_allocated_gpu: 12.1GB
kernel_switches: 224 count
kv_cache_gpu: 6.3GB
kv_cache_cpu: 2.1GB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.18
prefix_hit_rate_prewarm: 0.12
prefix_hit_rate_postwarm: 0.48 (after warmup window)
OOM_events: 3 (timestamps: 1912342710, 1912343154, 1912344002)
```

sara: prefix_hit_rate_prewarm at 12% is low — do we have key churn? any normalization differences between clients?

devon: yes — found two main sources: (1) trailing whitespace + punctuation differences from frontend serialization, (2) user-specific session id appended to prompt for a small subset. normalized keys fixed ~30% of that delta.

maria: interesting. what about evict TTLs? were we using uniform TTLs for all prefix buckets?

devon: we had a 10m default TTL, but urgent prefixes (completion seeds) had 2m TTL. Simulation that used dynamic TTL by size and recency reduced fragmentation slightly.

chris: propose experiment matrix: vary GPU/CPU cache ratio (60/40, 70/30, 80/20), TTLs (2m,5m,10m), and enable compaction sweep every N minutes (N=1,5,15). measure: peak resident, fragmentation, prewarm hit rate, mean latency.

sara: also add a kernel-stability flag: prefer stable kernel selection for seq lengths that flip a lot. sacrificing ~2-5% throughput could avoid spilling allocations.

devon: ran 60/40 with 5m TTL and compaction 5m — peak resident dropped 9%, fragmentation 0.11 -> 0.07, prewarm hit 12%->36%, no OOMs in 8h run.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: started canary with cache-ratio=0.6, ttl-default=300s, compaction_interval=300s on 3 nodes at 1912344200

maria: nice. any unexpected regression in latency tail?

devon: p95 latency increased by ~30ms for cold requests due to more CPU->GPU transfers when the CPU cache had larger share — but steady-state p50/p90 unchanged.

chris: tradeoff looks acceptable for canary. long-term: we should reduce key churn and add a small prefetcher for top-K prefixes per user cohort to accelerate warmup.

sara: and add a normalization step server-side for prompt canonicalization. small CPU cost but huge hit-rate gains. also consider TTL-tiering: shorter TTL for low-reuse prefixes and longer TTL for top-K frequent keys.

devon: did a rough calculation: if we move from 70/30 -> 60/40 and enable normalization + prefetch of top 200 prefixes per model, unit token cost drops ~6% because of fewer spills and kernel fallback churn.

maria: can we simulate worst-case churn (many unique prefixes per minute) to see when LRU degenerates?

devon: yes, I ran a synthetic churn test: 1k unique prefixes/sec for 30 minutes. LRU degraded — fragmentation climbed to 0.28, eviction churn caused 7% extra kernel switches and 2 OOMs. Adding a soft cap on new-key admission rate (token-bucket) solved it in sim.

chris: add admission-control + backpressure on route when new-key rate > X. Also surface a metric in console: new_prefix_rate and admitted_prefix_rate.

sara: for GPU memory, also consider compacting small allocations into slab arenas to lower fragmentation; we have a prototype allocator that reduced fragmentation by half in microbenchmarks. can we wire it to canary?

devon: plan: (1) enable server-side normalization, (2) set GPU/CPU cache ratio to 60/40 on canary, (3) compaction interval 5m, (4) admission-control throttle when new_prefix_rate>500/min, (5) enable slab allocator prototype on 25% of canary nodes. rolling out now.

maria: create a short dashboard with the four metrics (fragmentation_ratio, new_prefix_rate, prefix_hit_rate, kernel_switches) and alert if OOM_count>0 or fragmentation>0.2

infra-bot: alert-rule-created: /dashboards/eviction-sim-1912345678 (owner: devex)

chris: one more note — kernel selection logs show a lot of short-lived fallback to small-seq kernels when KV cache misses cause input sequence padding to change. normalize padding and use stable kernel hint to avoid that oscillation. -> I'll file a tiny change.

devon: thanks. will update the canary and capture traces. next checkpoint in 6 hours; if no OOMs and prewarm hit>30% we promote config to broader pool. :thumbsup:

sara: :rocket:
